## Proof: no live caller of the inbound absence-probe port (AC1)

Run per AGENTS.md with BOTH methods, since an empty Serena result alone is not trustworthy.

**Semantic (Serena, Pyright-backed).** `find_referencing_symbols` on `SupportsAbsenceProbe`
and on `SupportsAbsenceProbe/probe_remote` in `_backend.py` both returned EMPTY. Confirmed
this is a real result and not a stale/missing index: `find_symbol` resolves the same symbol
in the same file (Class `SupportsAbsenceProbe`, child Method `probe_remote`), so the file
IS indexed.

**String grep.** A repo-wide grep for `probe_remote|SupportsAbsenceProbe|ProbeBranch|
ProbeResult|ProbeConfigError|inbound_probe|classify_probe_response` returns hits ONLY in:
(a) the port surface itself, (b) tests of that surface, (c) docs/ADR/comment prose. No
production call site outside the port exists.

**Dynamic-load check (the case the LSP cannot see).** `inbound_probe.py`'s own docstring
claims it is "loaded by filename elsewhere", and `reconcile_helpers.py`'s docstring lists
`inbound_probe.py` among the siblings it loads by path. Both are STALE. There is no
`lazy_load("inbound_probe")`, no `_load(... "inbound_probe.py")`, and no
`spec_from_file_location` / `import_module` naming it anywhere in `src/` or `tests/` —
`reconcile_helpers._load` is only called for `config.py` and `alert_store.py`. The
docstrings were left behind when bug 3b5f removed `route_inbound_probe`. Correcting them
is folded into this ticket's blast radius.

**False-positive excluded.** `_commands/_init_probe.py::probe_remote_branch` matches the
grep but is UNRELATED — it probes a git remote BRANCH during `rebar init`.

**Live surface deliberately NOT touched.** The OUTBOUND probe is separate and live:
`_apply_outbound_probe`, the `(outbound, probe)` typed-dispatch arm, and `MutationKind.probe`
under `Direction.outbound`. Only the INBOUND `(inbound, probe)` chain is dormant. Deletion
detection likewise stays outbound (`outbound_differ._safe_get_issue` + `binding_walk`).

**Conclusion:** the port is provably dead. The deletion is safe and behavior-neutral.

## BLOCKED on the claim gate (no code was changed)

Work stopped before touching code, because this ticket cannot be claimed without `--force`:

  f020 (this ticket)  -- certified plan-review attestation EARNED (PASS, signed)
    |
    +-- parent epic 5796-d1f8-870f-4dc1 -- claim cascades here; it is `open` and
        needs its own attestation, but `review-plan 5796` fast-fails INDETERMINATE
        ("not-claimable"), because
          |
          +-- 5796 `depends_on` e369-a449-4773-48fb, which is still `in_progress`
              (57 of its 58 descendants are closed; the holdout is
               bug 8390-32f7-e4b8-48a1, `in_progress` and actively held by a
               different live session).

So the gate is unblockable from here by legitimate means: earning 5796's attestation
requires closing e369, which requires another session's in-flight bug to land. The only
overrides are `claim --force` or re-modelling the `5796 depends_on e369` link — both
operator judgment calls, not routine agent moves, so neither was taken.

Plan remediation completed pre-claim (the sanctioned revise -> review -> claim loop):
the description now states DELETE as the decision, demotes the re-home option to a
rejected alternative with the reviewer's mechanism findings folded in, and enumerates the
full blast radius including every test file that breaks on deletion; `file_impact` is
declared over all 26 files. Plan review is PASS + signed.

**To resume:** a fresh, provisioned worktree with no changes is at
`../f020-delete-absence-probe` (branch `f020-delete-absence-probe`). Once e369 closes,
run `review-plan 5796` -> `claim f020` and execute the deletion as specified.
